subject: SLO capacity & throughput checklist: next steps
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@greenleaf.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: perf targets & workload details (GreenLeaf PoC)

Connor / Vivek — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying items so our infra team can size the PoC: 

1) Business SLOs we care about (please confirm):
   - 95th percentile latency for streaming responses: < 250 ms per chunk for 128-token chunks
   - End-to-end response time for full responses (avg 600 tokens): < 800 ms at steady-state
   - Availability target: 99.9% during business hours

2) Workload shape (we gave a high-level view on the call):
   - Peak concurrency: up to ~60 concurrent chat sessions during peak (US East)
   - Steady-state concurrency: ~12 concurrent sessions
   - Average tokens per request: 400–700 (varies by prompt)
   - Streaming is mandatory for UX; clients expect progressive chunks every ~120 tokens

Ask: could you provide a simple throughput sizing (tokens/sec and QPS) and whether we should start on Hosted or Dedicated for the PoC? Also, do you need sample traffic logs or example request/response sizes from us?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short 20-min sync if that helps.

— Sara
Sara Lin
Product Manager, GreenLeaf Health
Sara.Lin@greenleaf.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: perf targets & workload details (GreenLeaf PoC)

Sara — thanks for the clear summary. Recap + next steps from our side below. I'm attaching a quick capacity_estimate.xlsx with a couple of sizing scenarios (conservative / recommended).

Quick answers:
- We can meet the 95p streaming chunk latency target (<250ms) with our hosted API at your expected steady-state traffic, but for headroom during peak bursts we recommend Dedicated for the PoC if you expect sustained peaks above ~40 QPS.

- Sizing assumptions used in the attachment:
  * Avg request size: 550 tokens
  * Avg chunk size for streaming: 128 tokens
  * Avg tokens/sec served per GPU (quantized LLM variant): 60k tokens/sec (best-effort estimate; depends on model choice)
  * Recommended initial concurrency capacity (dedicated): 48 concurrent streams to cover 95% of peaks at 60 concurrent max

Clarifying questions for you (please answer inline):
1) Can you confirm the true peak concurrent sessions vs. peak QPS? You mentioned ~60 sessions — are those long-lived streaming sessions or short chat bursts?
2) What fraction of requests will be short (<=128 tokens) vs long (>512 tokens)?
3) Are there any strict tail latency SLAs outside business hours?

Next steps:
- If you can share a 24-hour sample request distribution (counts by token-length bucket), Vivek can run a more precise batch/caching analysis and update the attachment.
- If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min technical sizing call tomorrow.

Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com
Attachment: capacity_estimate.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@greenleaf.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: perf targets & workload details (GreenLeaf PoC)

Adding some technical color from the inference/ops side — trying to keep this actionable for your infra folks.

Summary of what we'll need to produce a firm sizing and quote:
- Token distribution histogram (per-hour for a typical day) OR a sample log with timestamp, token_count, and streaming_enabled flag; 24–72 hours is ideal.
- Desired tail percentile to engineer to (95p vs 99p) and whether the SLA applies to streaming chunk latency or full-response time.
- Any region constraints (we'll assume us-east first).

Preliminary sizing notes (based on Connor's assumptions and our benchmarking):
- Model variant: recommending a 7B–13B open variant quantized to int8 for cost/throughput balance.
- Per-GPU sustained throughput (typical): ~55k tokens/sec for 13B q8; ~90k tokens/sec for optimized 7B q4x (varies by sequence length).
- For streaming UX (128-token chunks), 95p chunk latency under 250ms requires maintaining per-request dispatch latency <60ms and token generation throughput sufficient to ensure steady chunk delivery — this is operationally harder at high concurrency.

Sizing worked example (conservative):
- Peak: 60 concurrent streaming sessions, avg generation rate per session 20 tokens/sec -> ~1,200 tokens/sec peak -> ~1.2M tokens per 1000s -> rough GPU count = ceil(1,200 / 55,000) = 1 GPU (but concurrency and tail latency suggest 2 for headroom)
- Steady-state: 12 concurrent @ 20 tokens/sec -> 240 tokens/sec -> fits comfortably on hosted instances (0.01 of a GPU sustained), but we size by latency not tokens alone

Operational recommendations:
- Start PoC on Dedicated with 2 GPUs to ensure headroom for peaks and safe 95p streaming latency.
- Enable prefix caching for frequent prompt starts (if you have templates or common system prompts). That can reduce tokens served by up to 25% for canonical flows.
- Configure autoscaling with a fast scale-up path (minutes) and a conservative scale-down to avoid thrash.

If you can drop a 24-hour sample log (CSV), I'll run a quick script and return a revised estimate by EOD tomorrow.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Inference Performance
Redwood Inference
Attachment referenced: none (used local perf bench data)

Thanks all — this is very helpful. Attaching our final SLO matrix (slo_matrix.pdf) and a 24-hour sample traffic CSV that contains timestamp, token_count, and session_id. A few quick answers inline: 

- Peak concurrent sessions are long-lived (10–20 minute streams in many cases) — we see spikes to ~65 during morning ramp on weekdays.
- Token distribution: ~35% short (<128), ~45% mid (128–512), ~20% long (>512).
- We want to engineer to 95th percentile for streaming chunk latency and 99th percentile for full-response latencies during business hours.

Next steps from our side:
1) Please review the attached sample CSV and update your capacity_estimate.xlsx with a recommended PoC config (we prefer Dedicated for predictability).
2) Can you provide a rough PoC cost estimate (monthly) for the 2-GPU config you suggested?
3) Let's book the 30-min sizing call next Tue 11:00am ET — I can invite our infra lead.

If you prefer, feel free to reply with a short proposal and I'll convert to an internal request.

— Sara
Sara Lin
